Package hadur117.core.move

Class ClinchBreak

java.lang.Object
hadur117.core.move.ClinchBreak
public final class ClinchBreak extends Object
MOVE-75: getting out of contact with the enemy.

Once the two robots touch, the surf and the orbit can hold us there: near a wall or in a corner their wall-smoothed heading bends back toward the enemy, the engine stops a robot that drives into another one, and we stand still at point-blank range while it fires (the easy-robot dodge study, docs/bench/easy-dodge-study.md: 25 ticks a battle within 60 px against the robots BeepBoop scores 98% on, 8 for BeepBoop, and half the bullet damage we take inside 200 px). No dodge works at that range; the only answer is to leave.

While active, the drive is the heading that ends furthest from the enemy: of the headings within SPREAD of straight away from it, the one whose straight run of up to RUN px (cut short at a wall) ends furthest from where the enemy is now. Such a heading never points into the enemy, so the engine never stops us for it. We drive whichever end of the robot already points away, turning it onto the heading, so the first tick already moves.

It starts inside START px, centre to centre, and ends past RELEASE. Deterministic and stateless apart from that latch.
